result.title: "Not just small men" - how healthcare is failing women, and what can be done
result.description:
Women spend 25% more of their lives in poor health than men and are 50% more likely to die of a heart attack than a male patient.
The statistics are staggering - but there are some relatively simple and cost-effective ways healthcare systems can improve the situation.
Lucy Perez of the McKinsey Health Institute sets out the challenges and talks us through these potential solutions.

result.title: Uncertainty is proving a heavy tax, says S&P Global’s chief economist
result.description:
Policy uncertainty is acting as a drag on the global economy, says Paul Gruenwald, Global Chief Economist of S&P Global Ratings, as businesses and individuals hold back from spending because they don’t know what’s coming. 

Gruenwald is a member of the World Economic Forum’s Chief Economists Community,  which convenes experts to deepen understanding of current economic developments and identify policy priorities in the face of unprecedented levels of uncertainty.

result.title: What’s an ‘AI-first’ company? The CEO of Workera explains
result.description:
Plenty of companies are using artificial intelligence – but how many are AI-first? And what’s the difference?

Here, Workera CEO Kian Katanforoosh talks us through the three levels of AI integration – AI-enabled, AI-first and AI-native – and explains how executives can better embed #AI in their own businesses. (Hint: it’s by using it more themselves.)

A report from the World Economic Forum, The AI-First Operating System: A Blueprint for Operating and Business Model Innovation, explores how AI-first enterprises are rethinking #business models, workflows and decision-making. Read more: https://www.weforum.org/publications/the-ai-first-operating-system-a-blueprint-for-operating-and-business-model-innovation

result.title: AI and Jobs series: How entry level jobs are changing in an AI era
result.description:
Entry-level jobs provide a special window into the wider changes we'll see to job design and skill development. In this episode of Meet the Leader, Peter Brown of PwC explains how entry-level roles are transforming and breaks down new research on what employers really want from entry-level workers now. He also shares how these roles can continue to serve as training grounds for career skills like collaboration, critical thinking, and relationship building and why a thoughtful redesign of these roles will be key to future leadership development. Top names from our Chief People Officer community also share the advice new grads need to know in a fast-changing job market.
Key takeaways:

The most dire headlines about entry-level jobs are not yet backed up by data.
Employers are increasingly prioritizing applied experience and skills over degrees alone.
Employers are expecting more 'seniorized' skills earlier.
New grads should focus on outcomes rather than tasks and look for ways to build human skills on purpose.
Peter Brown is PwC’s global workforce leader and a co-author of the World Economic Forum report Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Entry-Level Work. Subscribe for more conversations on leadership, the future of work, and the biggest trends shaping business. This is the third episode in a 3-part series on AI and jobs.

result.title: Clean energy is the economic success story of the 21st century
result.description:
In today’s era of economic volatility and sluggish growth, the clean energy sector stands out as a global success story, creating jobs and driving economic growth around the world. 

China’s dominance in manufacturing has driven down the cost of #solar panels and wind turbines, but its scale is causing smaller players to erect trade barriers as they try to compete, says Kelly Sims Gallagher, Dean of The Fletcher School at Tufts University. Healthy competition is good news for this sector’s future, she argues. But who will provide it? 

Kelly Sims Gallagher joined a panel at this year’s Annual Meeting of the New Champions to discuss China’s #energy system and its future trajectory. You can watch the session here: https://www.weforum.org/meetings/annual-meeting-of-the-new-champions-2026/sessions/inside-china-s-energy-system/
